Cranking 90s
KRANK-ing NYN-teez
verb phrase (Gen Alpha slang)
Fortnite building slang from competitive play around 2018–19: a rapid sequence of wall, ramp, and floor placed while turning ninety degrees, repeated to climb high above an opponent in seconds. "Cranking" (turning hard, as with a crank) plus 90s (the ninety-degree turns). Mastering 90s took hours of practice in creative mode, and "he can crank 90s" became a mark of skill; the phrase outlived its technical meaning as kid slang for doing anything fast and well. Fortnite added a no-building mode, Zero Build, in March 2022.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Cranking 90s is a fast Fortnite building trick — spinning and stacking ramps and walls to rise above the other player. Gen Alpha kids practice it for hours and brag about speed. The Christian observation: the boast underneath is a boast about skill earned by practice, and Scripture honors that. "Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings" (Pro 22:29). Bezaleel was filled with skill for craftsmanship; the Levite musicians were "skilful"; diligence in small things is a virtue the Bible praises again and again. But Scripture also ranks practice: "bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things" (1Ti 4:8). A boy who can crank 90s in his sleep but has never memorized a psalm has practiced the lesser thing. And building has its own warning in the gospel: count the cost before you build a tower (Luk 14:28), and build on the Rock, not on sand (Mat 7:24). A father can tell a five-year-old: "It takes lots of practice to build fast in a game. God wants us to practice good things too — like saying kind words and learning Bible verses — so we get really good at them."

Webster 1828 Definition

Fortnite building technique (c. 2018–19): rapid stacked ramps and walls on ninety-degree turns — practiced skill Scripture honors, ranked below the practice of godliness.

expand to see more

CRANKING 90s, v. phr. (Fortnite competitive slang, c. 2018–present) Building rapidly upward with repeated wall-ramp placements on ninety-degree turns. "He cranked 90s and got high ground."

Related: high ground, box up, edit, sweat (a highly skilled, intense player).

Extended kid usage: doing something very fast and skillfully.

Decode for parents: a sign of hours of practice — worth knowing how many.

Webster 1828, the root — CRANK, n. Literally, a bend or turn. Hence, an iron axis with the end bent like an elbow, for moving a piston, the saw in a saw-mill, etc., and causing it to rise and fall at every turn.

Key Scripture

Pro 22:29 — "Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men."

1Ti 4:8 — "For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come."

Luk 14:28 — "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?"

Mat 7:24 — "Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:"

Modern Corruption

Cranking 90s is skill bought by practice, which Scripture honors; the danger is practicing the lesser thing to the neglect of godliness, which profits in all things.

expand to see more

There is honest discipline in a child who drills a hard skill until his hands know it. The question is where the discipline is going. Many Gen Alpha boys have logged more practice hours on Fortnite builds than on any instrument, sport, or book, and the game is designed to reward exactly that devotion.

Praise the diligence and redirect some of it. Ask your son what he can practice that will last — a verse, a skill with his hands, a kindness repeated until it is habit. Bodily exercise profits a little; Fortnite exercise profits less; godliness profits in all things.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

English crank (to turn) + 90s (ninety-degree turns) → competitive Fortnite building (2018–19) → kid slang for fast skill.

expand to see more

Old English cranc — a bent handle for turning → to crank

2018–19: competitive Fortnite building technique

Practiced in creative mode; a mark of skill on the playground

March 2022: Zero Build mode removes building for some players
